generalized_learning.generalized_failure_pattern: A presentation or transport layer can preserve readable labels while discarding canonical identity needed by a later canonical route, filter or action boundary.
generalized_learning.plausible_wrong_implementation: Map display labels only, allow homonymous resources to look correct, and conclude that no canonical destination exists because the identifier was lost before the navigation decision.
trigger_signals: presentation mapping/view-model between source and consumer
display label differs from canonical identity
conditional navigation or mutation depends on identity

reusable_control.procedure: Use two deliberately distinct canonical identities with the same display label, traverse the mapping boundary and observe the downstream canonical consumer; also test a missing-identity case.

generalized_learning.prevention_rule: When a requirement is conditional on a canonical destination, enumerate candidate canonical routes/filters/actions before declaring none and preserve every identity field required by the selected destination through intermediate transforms.
generalized_learning.detection_rule: Adversarially vary canonical identity independently from display labels and observe the final navigation/action boundary; reject fabricated destinations when identity is absent.

transfer_cases.case: Two resources share one label but have distinct canonical identities before a navigable consumer.
A capability claim is checked against the canonical route/filter inventory before stating that no destination exists.

skill_changes.change: The delivery controller explicitly derives semantic identity propagation controls from canonical-path requirements.
Re-audit readiness enforces cumulative rejection closure and semantic evidence before another independent audit.
